public_rationale: Public profitability claims from Midjourney and HeyGen predated the post. They substantially challenge the assertion that there had never been an example outside Nvidia and training-data suppliers. However, the original claim specifies no accounting basis, and the company statements do not define profit. The required money-claim rule therefore prevents a formal contradicted verdict.
limitations: These are attributed company claims, not verified net-income accounts.
The historical starting point is approximate.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Three years in, there is no profitable generative AI company other than training-data firms and Nvidia.

statement.excerpt: Why isn’t there one, outside of the companies creating data to train the AI models, or Nvidia? We’re three years in, and we haven’t had one.

from_speaker: outside of the companies creating data to train the AI models, or Nvidia
our_interpretation: One refers to a profitable generative AI product company.
The phrase we haven't had one is cumulative: an earlier profitable company can challenge it even without proof of current profitability.
Three years is approximate. Use calendar 2022 through publication rather than inventing an exact anniversary.
Training-data suppliers and Nvidia are exclusions from the population, not conditional antecedents.
The statement specifies no accounting basis.
criteria.support_condition: Sufficiently comprehensive, comparable financial records show no qualifying profitable company during the target period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A qualifying company outside the stated exclusions demonstrably earned company-wide profit at some point during the target period on a basis matching the claim.
